models.name: EnsembleSleepNet
models.note: The 3 sub-models and their 9 channels run side by side, and every dist point cuts all branches at the same depth. Every dist point after the raw signals also needs the spectrograms computed on the wearable (about 1.1 M MACs, included); the 172 handcrafted features per channel are not counted.

splits.label: Raw signals, 9 channels
splits.note: The phone computes the spectrograms (STFT) and the handcrafted features.

splits.label: Raw + spectrograms + handcrafted features (all 3 input views)
splits.note: The wearable computes the spectrograms (counted as about 1.1 M MACs) and the handcrafted features (not counted).

splits.label: Per-channel CNNs after their first pooling layer (27 branches)

models.params_note: excludes the 3 sub-model heads used only when a sub-model runs alone (1,295 parameters)

models.name: LSM-Base
models.note: Only the encoder runs at inference, on all 180 tokens (nothing is masked).

splits.label: Minute-level features
splits.note: The wearable already computes these features; that cost is not counted.

splits.label: Final embedding (average over all tokens)
splits.note: Enough for classification. Imputation and forecasting need the per-token output from the previous dist point.

models.name: SleepFM encoder
models.note: Each inference covers a 5-min chunk of all 23 channels. The disease and sleep-stage heads run on the phone over the whole night.

splits.note: The paper's disease and sleep-stage heads need the 5-s outputs of transformer layer 6, so this point can't serve those tasks and is never picked as the best choice.

models.name: SensorLM-B sensor tower
models.note: Only the sensor encoder would run on the wearable; the text encoder and caption decoder run on the phone.

splits.label: Final sensor embedding (average + projection)
splits.note: Enough for zero-shot classification and retrieval. Captioning needs all 1872 tokens.
